sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill for a house in Rochester?
sections.html:
The City of Rochester sends one bill that covers the city and the Rochester City School District, and Monroe County sends a second bill. A house inside the city limits therefore carries two separate tax accounts, and a buyer or title company will ask about both.

City bills go out by mail each July to owners who do not pay through a mortgage escrow. Under New York Real Property Tax Law section 922, the owner still has to pay on time if a bill never arrives. Monroe County bills separately and mails its bill on December 31 for city properties. For county questions, call the Monroe County Real Property Tax Service Office.

Three city offices matter if you are about to sell:

  • Bureau of Assessment, City Hall Room 101A, 30 Church Street: values, exemptions and assessment complaints.
  • Treasury Bureau, City Hall, 30 Church Street: unpaid taxes, payment agreements and the amount owed on a given parcel.
  • Rochester Water Department and the Municipal Code Violations Bureau: water charges and code fines, which the city's online property tool does not show in full.

Rochester splits the city and school bill into four installments: July 31, September 30, January 31 and March 31. The 2026 cycle runs July 31 and September 30, 2026, then January 31 and March 31, 2027. If an earlier installment is still open, check whether the balance rolled forward before you list the house.

A late installment collects interest at 1 percent per month. If a deadline lands on a weekend, the following Monday is the cutoff. The city encourages electronic payment. Mailed payments go to the Binghamton post office box named on the bill coupon, with the check made out to the City Treasurer and the installment coupon enclosed. Payments under a tax agreement are the exception: those go straight to the Treasury Bureau at City Hall.

Throw away any old return label from a prior year, since the city's mailing address changed. An owner paying in full by July 31 should send the first installment coupon, because the city built that coupon to handle either a full payment or the first quarter.

A one, two or three family house in Rochester is taxed at the homestead rate, which for 2026-27 combines to $18.2157 per $1,000 of assessed value once city, school, county and the Pure Waters capital charge are added. Everything that is not a one to three family home or some vacant land pays the non-homestead rate.

The city bill also carries per-frontage-foot charges for roadway plowing, street cleaning, sidewalk plowing and hazard sidewalk replacement, and a yearly refuse fee for houses with up to three units. That fee is $411 for a one-family house, $827 for two families and $917 for three. Water is billed separately unless the account becomes substantially delinquent, at which point it can land on the tax bill. Code enforcement charges can be added to the bill too.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Rochester assessment?
sections.html:
File a complaint with the Rochester Board of Assessment Review by 8 p.m. Eastern on the third Tuesday in March. In 2027 that Tuesday is March 16, and the form has to be received at the Bureau of Assessment, City Hall Room 101A, by that hour.

The assessment calendar runs in this order each year:

  • February 1: exemption applications and renewals are due, and the taxable status date falls here.
  • March 1: the tentative roll is filed with New York State.
  • Third Tuesday in March: complaint deadline. Hearings run through March and April.
  • May 1: the final roll is filed.
  • May 30: Small Claims Assessment Review filing deadline.
  • July 1 through January 1: informal assessment reviews are available.

The informal review window is the quiet option for an owner who missed the March deadline. Bring photos and a recent appraisal or comparable sales if you want the assessor to look at condition problems.

The city lists STAR, a senior citizen exemption, military service exemptions, a disability exemption, a capital improvement exemption and a clergy exemption. Every application has to reach the Bureau of Assessment by February 1, 2027. The Bureau runs an exemption hotline at 585-428-6994.

Income and age thresholds from the city's exemptions page:

  • Enhanced STAR: owner age 65 or older, or turning 65 by December 31, 2027, with household income up to $113,550 in 2025.
  • Senior citizen exemption: owner age 65 or older (or a surviving spouse 62 or older) with income up to $58,400 in the prior year, renewed each year.
  • Disability exemption: same $58,400 income cap, for owners receiving certain disability benefits or certified as legally blind.
  • Capital improvement: one and two family houses with at least $3,000 of qualifying improvements.

New STAR recipients get a check from New York State instead of a bill reduction, so they register with the state tax department. If you have been receiving a senior or disability exemption, know that the city can add a supplemental tax when a prior owner's exemption ends through a transfer or death.

Rochester suspended its tax lien sales in 2020 until further notice, but the lien itself still exists. A lien starts when the annual tax is levied, and once the bill has gone unpaid for one year it counts as delinquent.

When the city ran its sales, an owner got a notice and had twenty days to clear the debt, and a buyer of the lien (the city used American Tax Funding Services) collected the debt from then on. Owners could apply for a delinquency agreement with the Director of Finance at least twenty days before a sale date. Liens did not qualify for sale if a payment agreement was in force, if bankruptcy law restricted enforcement, or if a tax certiorari proceeding for the same year was pending. The state redemption rule for delinquent liens is a two-year period under RPTL section 1110, which a taxing district can lengthen for homes.

The Treasury Bureau handles delinquency questions at 585-428-6940. Ask it for a payoff figure in writing before you accept an offer on a house with unpaid years.

sections.h2: Settling unpaid taxes when you sell
sections.html:
Your title company asks the Treasury Bureau for the amount owed and pays it from your sale proceeds at closing, so a delinquent balance does not block a sale. The balance does reduce what you receive.

The city's online property information tool is updated nightly and should not be used for final billings or closings, because unbilled taxes, fines and fees may exist. Three separate calls cover the gaps: the Treasury Bureau for taxes, the Water Department at 585-428-5990 for water, and the Municipal Code Violations Bureau for fines and tickets. If the house has inherited or exemption history, mention that to the title company early so a supplemental tax does not surprise anyone.

For a sale where you want to skip repairs, that list is also your pre-listing checklist. A buyer paying cash for the house as it stands still needs a clean payoff letter, and getting it before the contract is signed shortens the closing.

Rochester is a renter-heavy city, with 38.1 percent of homes owner-occupied. The July 2025 population estimate is 206,108, down 2.4 percent from the April 2020 base. Median value of owner-occupied homes is $139,600 and median gross rent is $1,081. Heavy lake effect snow, averaging just over 100 inches a year, is worth remembering when a buyer's inspector looks at roofs and gutters, and values on a Browncroft or Charlotte street can look very different from the citywide median.

faqs.q: Do I owe Monroe County tax on a Rochester house?
faqs.a: Yes. Rochester properties get a Monroe County bill in addition to the city and school bill, and the county bill is issued on December 31. The city bill does not include county charges, so call the Monroe County Real Property Tax Service Office at 585-753-1125 for county balances.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rochester house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid amount, with interest at 1 percent per month on late installments, is paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasury Bureau for a current payoff before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: Is there a way to pay overdue Rochester taxes over time?
faqs.a: Yes. The Director of Finance can approve a delinquency or tax agreement for eligible owners, and a parcel under an active agreement is protected from lien sale. Call the Treasury Bureau at 585-428-6940 to ask whether you qualify.

faqs.q: Which Rochester exemption deadline is next?
faqs.a: February 1, 2027, a Monday. Exemption applications and renewals for seniors, military service and disabled owners must be at the Bureau of Assessment by then.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to challenge my Rochester assessment?
faqs.a: 8 p.m. Eastern on the third Tuesday in March, which is March 16, 2027, with the form received at City Hall Room 101A. Missing it leaves informal review between July 1 and January 1 and a Small Claims Assessment Review filing by May 30.
